subject: Renewal + mid-contract expansion — Skybridge usage surge
messages:
From: Ari Levinson <ari@skybridge.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@skybridge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on renewal math — mid-quarter spike

Hi Rachel,

We're wrapping up our internal forecasting and wanted to flag a usage spike — a new feature rolled into Prod last week has increased token consumption by ~45% month-over-month. Our renewal is due next month and we don't want to be constrained by current commit structure.

Questions:
- Can Redwood accommodate a short-term uplift (temporary committed top-up) that converts to a permanent add if usage persists?
- What's the impact to pricing tiers and discounting if we annualize a mid-contract increase?
- Any fast procurement path (PO + amend) you recommend so we don't exceed rate limits?

I've copied contracts in case we need a quick addendum. Happy to jump on 20–30 min today if that helps.

Thanks,
Ari Levinson
Head of Platform
Skybridge AI

--
Attachment: skybridge_usage_report_q3.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Levinson <ari@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, contracts@skybridge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on renewal math — mid-quarter spike

Hi Ari —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the report. Short answer: yes, we can support a mid-term uplift and provide two pragmatic paths depending on how Skybridge wants to manage cost and procurement friction. High-level options below. I'll follow up with numbers from Ben.

Option A — Temporary top-up (fast):
- 30–90 day committed top-up at current dedicated rates (no annual re-annualization)
- Minimal paperwork: PO + one-page amendment
- No changes to renewal date
- Good if you want immediate capacity protection while you observe consumption

Option B — Mid-contract annualize (preferred for predictability):
- Convert top-up to an increased annual commit, pro-rated to the existing renewal date
- Eligibility for tiered discounting applies to combined commit (we can apply a modest uplift discount for the incremental units)
- Requires an amendment + updated SOW; procurement lead time 7–10 business days typically

Questions for you to pick:
1) Would Skybridge prefer immediate protection (Option A) or are you leaning to annualize (Option B)?
2) Target committed units (or an expected % increase) so Ben can model pricing bands.

If you want, we can provision a temporary burst pool today and run the pricing workbook against your Q3 numbers; Ben — copying you to run the numbers and propose a concrete amendment.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Levinson <ari@skybridge.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, contracts@skybridge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on renewal math — mid-quarter spike

Ari — thanks for the data. I ran a quick model with the attached workbook (redwood_skybridge_pricing_workbook.xlsx) based on the ~45% uplift you mentioned. Key notes:

- If you take Option A (30d top-up): incremental unit price = $0.0018/token equivalent; no discount layering.
- If you annualize (Option B) and increase commit by 40% pro-rated to renewal: blended effective discount on incremental units = ~12% (because combined commit hits the next band).
- We can offer a one-time conversion credit equal to the unused portion of a 30d top-up if you convert within 60 days. That keeps Option A low-friction.
- Procurement path: PO + standard amendment. For annualization we'll need a signed amendment and a new SOW for billing.

I've included a short sensitivity table in the workbook (tab: "sensitivity") showing breakpoints at +20%, +40%, +60%. If you share an expected run rate for the next 90 days I can lock a recommendation and exact contract language for the amendment.

Marissa — are we comfortable offering a 12% uplift discount band conversion and the conversion credit as a standard play here, or should we reserve that for a higher ARR threshold?

Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_skybridge_pricing_workbook.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

From: Ari Levinson <ari@skybridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@skybridge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on renewal math — mid-quarter spike

Thanks Ben & Rachel — this is helpful. Skybridge preference is: start with Option A immediately (fast PO) and convert to Option B if the new feature maintains the higher run-rate after 60 days. The conversion credit sounds perfect.

Requested next steps from our side:
- I will issue a PO for a 30-day top-up today to contracts@redwood.ai.
- Can you provision the temporary buffer (capacity + rate limits) by EOD?
- Please send the draft one-page amendment and conversion terms so our procurement can pre-clear it with legal.

We expect to know whether the uplift will persist by mid-November. If it does, we'll move to annualize.

Thanks,
Ari
